cases.label: trailing space and case on the country side: country codes 'CA ' and 'mx' joined by province codes 'ca' and 'MX'
cases.reasoning: The fixed cases put the variant on the province side only. Here the CountryRegion key itself is stored as 'CA ' (nvarchar keeps the space) and 'mx'. SQL Server pads and compares case-insensitively, so 'ca' joins 'CA ' and 'MX' joins 'mx'. The conversion must trim and fold the country side too.

cases.label: expansions: province code 'Æ' against country 'AE' and 'ß' against 'SS', with 'ae' and 'ss' as case-only controls
cases.reasoning: Windows collation rules (used by SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS for nvarchar) treat 'Æ' as equal to 'AE' and 'ß' as equal to 'ss'. The ICU root collation at strength 2 gives 'æ' its own primary weight (not equal to 'ae') while 'ß' = 'ss' differs only at the tertiary level. The engines may disagree on whether the 'Æ' province joins. Same join as Purchasing.vVendorWithAddresses, whose conversion was corrected after this input differed; this conversion still uses rtrim + the ICU collation alone.

cases.label: compatibility forms: full-width U+FF35 U+FF33 against 'US' and the Kelvin sign U+212A followed by 'E' against 'KE', with 'ke' as a case-only control
cases.reasoning: SQL Server collations without _WS are width-insensitive, so full-width 'ＵＳ' equals 'US'; U+212A KELVIN SIGN is canonically equivalent to 'K'. ICU at strength 2 ignores width (a tertiary difference) and normalises canonical equivalents. Either engine may treat one of these differently. Same join as Purchasing.vVendorWithAddresses, whose conversion was corrected after this input differed; this conversion still uses rtrim + the ICU collation alone.

cases.label: whitespace look-alikes: 'US' with a trailing no-break space (U+00A0), a trailing tab, a leading space, a soft hyphen (U+00AD) inside, and 'CA ' (a real trailing space)
cases.reasoning: SQL Server pads the shorter value with U+0020 before comparing, so only 'CA ' is certain to join. Whether U+00A0 compares equal to the pad space, and whether the soft hyphen U+00AD is ignorable, are collation rules; PostgreSQL rtrim(' ') removes U+0020 only and ICU treats U+00AD as ignorable and U+00A0 as a space variant. A tab and a leading space should join on neither engine. Same join as Purchasing.vVendorWithAddresses, whose conversion was corrected after this input differed; this conversion still uses rtrim + the ICU collation alone.

cases.label: accents and dotted/dotless I: 'ÜS' against 'US' (accent-sensitive); U+0131 and U+0130 followed by 'T' against 'IT', with 'it' as a case-only control
cases.reasoning: CI_AS is accent-sensitive, so 'ÜS' must not join 'US'. U+0131 (dotless i) and U+0130 (I with dot above) case-fold differently by rule set: Windows rules and ICU root may each match or not match 'IT'. 'it' joins on both. Same join as Purchasing.vVendorWithAddresses, whose conversion was corrected after this input differed; this conversion still uses rtrim + the ICU collation alone.

cases.label: an empty country code: province codes '' and ' ' both join country '' (trailing spaces ignored)
cases.reasoning: SQL Server compares '' and ' ' as equal (padding), so both provinces join the country whose code is ''. rtrim(' ') gives '' on PostgreSQL; this checks the empty-string edge of the rtrim + ICU equality and that '' is not treated as NULL. Same join as Purchasing.vVendorWithAddresses, whose conversion was corrected after this input differed; this conversion still uses rtrim + the ICU collation alone.
